dataset.name: Annual floodplain sediment deposition recorded using feldspar clay marker horizons along the East River, Colorado, 2015-2017
description: White feldspar clay was placed along 24 transects defining a ~9-km long study reach along the meandering snowmelt-dominated East River in Colorado, USA. Feldspar markers horizons were placed in the fall of 2015 and 2016 along transects with the space between them increasing with distance from the channel. Depths of floodplain deposition were measured the following summers of 2016 and 2017 following annual peak flow after peak snowmelt. This dataset includes individual and average measurements made in the field along with coordinates in NAD 83 UTM Zone 13.

measurementTechnique:
To quantify vertical accretion rates following peak flow conditions, we placed marker horizons composed of clay feldspar along channel-normal transects in the fall of 2014, 2015 and 2016. White feldspar clay was placed on the floodplain to create markers horizons to record the depth of annual floodplain deposition (Noe & Hupp, 2005). In 2014, ten marker horizons were installed across two meander bends in the vicinity of the Crested Butte, CO pump house. In 2015, 80 marker horizons were installed on 15 transects in both the upper and lower reaches of the floodplain. In 2016, we expanded the extent of the floodplain covered by marker horizon transects, installing 108 marker horizons along ten transects. To obtain better coverage closer to the channel in 2016, eighteen 25 x 150 cm rectangular marker horizons were placed 0 to 1.5 m from the edge of the bankfull channel. The remainder of the 2016 markers (90) were 25 x 25 cm in size located 3, 6, 9, 12, 36, and 60 meters from the channel. The square marker horizons were approximately were spacing increased with distance from the channel with approximately logarithmic spacing based on the expectation that the deposition rates should decrease exponentially with distance from the channel (Day et al., 2008). Marker horizon locations were surveyed using a Trimble differential global positioning system, R10 rover, and R10 base station to provide a post-processing accuracy within 1 cm. The elevation of each marker horizon was determined based on its location on the 2015 aerial lidar DEM with 0.5 meter resolution.
Minimal deposition occurred in 2015 and 2016, however following peak flow conditions in 2017, sedimentation was measured on marker horizons. For each of the square marker horizons, four squares approximately 3 x 3 cm were cut into the aggraded sediment and white feldspar from the four corners of a 15 x 15-cm square at the inner area of each square marker. Similarly, four squares were cut and extracted within the outer 20 cm of the rectangular marker horizons. The thickness of sediment above the marker horizon was measured at the center of each of the four sides of each extracted square and the arithmetic mean was calculated from all measurements to estimate the average deposition on each marker. Sediment thickness was averaged along rectangular markers at 0.2 m and 1.3 m from the channel on horizons not eroded by scour along point bars.
Transect names indicate the downstream distance from the beginning of the study reach followed by a dash and the measured distance from the channel.
